moments.text: Your partner forgetting the anniversary dinner was still hard for you.

skills_full.name: Naming the feeling out loud

skills_full.name: Repairing after a rough moment
skills_full.in_your_words: You apologise when things go off, explain yourself, and stay in the conversation. That can leave you feeling closer afterwards.

skills_full.name: Letting the talk go better
skills_full.in_your_words: You notice when the talk goes better than shouting ever did, and you stay with that kind of exchange. Your partner listening matters here.

moments.text: Skipping visiting your mother on Sunday was still hard for you.
You noticed you were exhausted and felt guilty all week.
You noticed guilt tells you rest has to be earned.
Your therapist suggested speaking to yourself as you would to a friend.
You rested on Saturday without doing anything for anyone.
When guilt came, you told yourself, you are allowed to be tired.
You called your mother instead of visiting and told her you needed a quiet weekend.
You called your mother instead of visiting, and she understood.
You took an evening off again.
You noticed guilt showed up and faded after an hour.
You finished one evening with nothing to earn.

skills_full.name: Talking to yourself like a friend

skills_full.name: Taking rest without earning it
skills_full.in_your_words: You take an evening off or rest on Saturday without doing anything for anyone. You are making space for rest even when guilt is in the background.

skills_full.name: Keeping a quiet weekend
skills_full.in_your_words: You choose a quieter plan, like calling instead of visiting, so you can have rest without pushing yourself. That helps you end the day with less strain.

skills_full.name: Resting without doing more
skills_full.in_your_words: You rested on Saturday without doing anything for anyone, and you finished one evening with nothing to earn. You let the time be enough as it is.
